Base & repricing

Did price visit a new range, or start living there?

11 chapters with worked investigations

01Price structure02Base & repricing03Supply zones04Demand & absorption05Holder rotation06Expansion & pullback07Continuation vs distribution08Swing lifecycle09Retracement references: 0.5 & 0.61810Comprehensive swing check11How to trade the swing

01Definition

A base repeatedly meets selling with buying. Repricing means trading persists around a different valuation range.

02Why it matters

A fast pump and an accepted new range can look similar at first.

03What to check

  • Time and repeated tests within the new range
  • Response to selling
  • Liquidity stability and coverage

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

The new range survives several tests with continuing activity.

Dangerous

Price briefly spikes higher, then returns to the old range.

05Beginner mistake

Calling every large move repricing.

06Takeaway

A new valuation needs acceptance.

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

After trading near 1.00, price spikes to 1.50, then spends hours between 1.30 and 1.40 through several sales. That can support a new working range more than a single print at 1.50. It still can fail later.

How to investigate it

Define the proposed range, time spent, number of distinct tests, sell sizes, and recovery. Check that pool coverage and liquidity remained comparable; a thinner pool can exaggerate both spikes and apparent rebounds. Record the lower boundary and behavior that would reject the base interpretation.

Check your reasoning — answered

Price touches 1.40 once with no continuing trades. Is that repricing? It is an isolated observed price, not evidence that participants sustained a new valuation range.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Swing

Compare observed persistence and liquidity, then inspect candle history. Estimated MC assumes the reported supply relationship remains valid.

Go deeper

There is no universal number of tests or duration that certifies acceptance. State your timeframe and evidence, then identify what would disprove the new-base hypothesis.
